brief: BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 8.8 from 9.3, still a Sell signal, even as hedge fund and FMS positioning readings run very bullish and global equity breadth has deteriorated to its worst since March 2026, with 400 S&P 500 stocks below their 50-day average beneath index strength concentrated in AI names. BofA's framing: markets stay risk-off until the dollar peaks, and the dollar is currently spiking on credit-event risk; fear of policy panic, including open-ended Treasury buybacks and yield-curve control, caps downside because policymakers cannot let yields derail the AI capex boom before the midterms, unless small- and mid-cap benchmarks break key levels. Separately, BofA casts the AI trade as a railroad-bubble repeat: AI capex, forecast at 3.5-4% of GDP in 2027, stays below railroads' roughly 5% GDP peak and chip prices are rising rather than deflating, but railroad booms were backstopped by falling Treasury yields, unlike today, and both historic railroad bubbles ended in credit crunches. BofA recommends adding bonds anyway, calling it 'buy humiliation,' citing historical entry points after negative long-run returns. Fund flows rotated into bonds, munis and tech; private-client cash allocation hit a record low.
